title: Apple Health Should Be the Gold Standard—But It Feels Stuck in the Past
body:
Apple Health should be the most advanced health and wellness platform out there. It’s Apple, after all—known for innovation, design, and pushing boundaries. But the reality? Using this app in 2025 feels like stepping back a decade.

Despite its integration with the iPhone and Apple Watch, Apple Health feels barebones next to competitors. It’s missing basic features that could transform it from a passive data collector into a truly helpful tool.
	•	No built-in calorie or macronutrient tracking. Why rely on third-party apps for such core health insights?
	•	The menstrual tracking is underwhelming. Minimal features, poor prediction accuracy, and no customization options. It feels like an afterthought.
	•	Exercise tracking with Apple Watch is frustrating. Stop at a red light during a run? The timer keeps going. Unlike other fitness platforms, there’s no intelligent auto-pause, so your stats get skewed—something so simple, yet missing.
	•	No smart feedback or personalized insights. The app gathers endless data but does nothing proactive with it. Where’s the coaching? Where’s the encouragement?
	•	No true goal-setting system or progress motivation. You can track things, but you don’t feel progress. The app doesn’t help you stay on track or push further.
	•	Still no way to log symptoms, moods, or notes contextually. For users managing chronic conditions or detailed wellness goals, this is a huge missed opportunity.

It’s like Apple Health is maintained just enough to not fall apart, but not nearly enough to lead the market. With Apple’s resources, this app could easily outshine every competitor. But right now, it’s trailing behind.

We want Apple Health to be the best. It’s time for a serious upgrade—one that reflects how people actually use health tech in their lives today.
